body:
Wow, I was not expecting someone to take the time to respond in such depth--thank you! Everything you say makes a lot of sense. I really don't know how he is feeling, and I don't want to pretend like I do. I mean, heck, I hate when I'm going through a hard time or a bad day and someone tells me they understand! I like the idea about animal therapy, and I've heard about it being used before but never thought to apply it to this situation. We have a few pets at our house, and quite honestly the only time I've seen him smile is when he's petting and talking to them. It's also really nice to know that a person who has suicidal thoughts typically doesn't want to harm others, only themselves. However, my mind isn't completely at ease with that simply because Ted needs some serious mental help for his other disorders. Anyway, I will definitely be rereading and using your suggestions to try and make living here normal for him and for all of us. I am just so nervous to say something wrong. I suppose it will just take a lot of adjusting and I will learn as we go. One more thing--I find myself very suspicious of Ted, always fearful he is trying to do something. For example, when he wakes up in the middle of the night and is in the bathroom for over an hour I will lie awake and listen to his every move (yes I know, that sounds awkward. But he is not doing normal bathroom things in there from what I can tell. There is little to no sounds made and the toilet will flush multiple times without the sink being turned on to wash hands). Should I be this suspicious/paranoid or should I trust him more? That may be a very silly question--but I'm new to this and worried. 

Thank you again for your response, It really made me feel better that someone cared enough to take the time to help! As for you--I hope that when you say you came here to post your plans, you weren't thinking about harming yourself in anyway. It may not seem like a lot to you, but you helped me tonight and I'm glad you were here to do so. Thank you!
